parts:
Hi,

will all probes ("HuEx-1_0-st-v2,main,A20070914,EP.cdf") to normalize

I am analysing 32 samples in a MAC with 2Gb.
Can I use the CDF file with all the probes for analysis in this
computer? Should I use the CDF files with the core or the Extended +
Core probesets from the initial step?

Thank you
Ana Grosso

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] ExonRmaPlm - memory error
parts:
Hi Ana.

You should be able to process 32 samples easily on a Mac with 2Gb.

You have control over the amount of memory used with the 'ram'
argument in the 'fit' method. By default, it is set to 1. You could
try setting it to something lower, such as:

fit(plmGene,verbose=verbose,ram=.5)

Basically, all that does is splits the fitting into more chunks, thus
requiring less memory for each chunk. It will probably only take a
small amount of extra time.

Also, check whether you have objects already loaded in your R session
that may be consuming some space.

Hope that helps.
Mark

This is what I suspected. When doing probe summarization, a so called
"monocell CDF" is needed. If missing, it is created automatically
from the main CDF. This is only done the very first time you use a
CDF never used before. When it is created, aroma.affymetrix will
always find it. You run into memory problem while aroma.affymetrix
tries to create this file.

You can create "manually" by doing:

cdf <- cdfEnsb; # or whatever CDF you are using in the PLM.
cdfM <- getMonocellCdf(cdf, ram=0.5, verbose=verbose);

As you see, this method also takes argument 'ram' so you can create
the monocell CDF on computers with small memory. If you still have
problems, try a smaller value on 'ram', or redo it in a fresh R
session before any data analysis. When you can do print(cdfM)
afterwards, you never have to do this again.

FYI, in next release the 'ram' argument to fit() will be passed down
to the internally called getMonocellCdf(), which hopefully will
increase your chances to succeed with Mark's suggestion.

Hope this helps

parts:
Hi,

I've committed a patch that is more memory efficient. In your case
you run out of memory while it validates the correctness of the
created file. Apply the patch (only needed once until next release):

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

Before you retry, make sure you remove the temporary CDF file:
annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-
st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2,U-Ensembl49,G-Affy,monocell.CDF.tmp

Sorry for the mess. We could send you a pre-created monocell CDF, but
I rather want to identify inefficiencies in aroma.affymetrix so others
can avoid this problem in the future.

Let us know how it goes.

Henrik
